title: Rotating and folded wordlist keys
question: Can rotating or folded expansions of 43 archived keys recover a known LP2 page opening?
reader_title: Keys that move or run forwards and backwards
reader_intro: A folded key runs forwards, then backwards: ABC becomes ABCCBA when the ends repeat, or ABCB when they do not. Moving where that sequence starts is a separate choice. Letters illustrate key positions, not manuscript text.

reader_test.input: 43 archived keys, written as rune numbers from 0 to 28, and the starts of 55 LP2 pages containing runes.
reader_test.action: For each key, shift the next cycle left or right, or run it forwards and backwards with or without repeating the ends. Try every starting place, subtract key numbers from rune numbers, and restart on each page.
reader_test.check: Compare each page’s first 12 output runes with nine already-decoded passage openings.

reader_finding: The full four-rule test checked 6,272 key settings on 55 LP2 pages containing runes. None matched any of the nine supplied 12-rune openings; the longest match was four runes.
reader_limit: This check looks only for these nine openings at page starts. Other text, later positions, keys or ways of using them remain untested.
reader_question: Could changing the key as it repeats reveal a familiar opening?
summary: Rotating/folded schedules produced no exact known opening across 6,272 settings and 55 pages.
finding: Zero of 3,104,640 exact comparisons match; the longest shared prefix is four runes. Planted controls and independent census pass.
limitations: Only four declared schedules, 43 keys, page starts and nine fixed openings. Different plaintexts, keys or key rules remain possible.
next_steps: Define a new key rule and an independently predicted continuation before testing it.

scope.representation: First 12 recognized GP29 runes per LP2-00–55 page, including headings; LP2-50 has no runes. Non-runes do not advance the key.
scope.procedure: Expand each key by left/right cycle rotation or forward/backward folding with/without repeated endpoints. Reduce to true period; test every phase; subtract scheduled key index modulo 29.
scope.parameters: 43 keys; four expansions; 6,272 settings; 55 pages; nine 12-rune openings; 3,104,640 comparisons.
scope.exclusions: Other keys, later positions, unknown openings, alternate signs, resets, interruptions, layers and language scoring.

review.reviewer: Independent page-record checker, all-case digest and planted controls

reproduction.environment: Python 3 standard library, no network or third-party packages; keep repository structure.

browser_followups.title: Replay folded keys with both end runes repeated
browser_followups.question: Does a key read forward and backward including both end runes recover one of nine known openings?
browser_followups.scope_change: Replay the historical fold-repeat-endpoints variant: all 618 distinct full key cycles and starting places, subtraction, page restarts, 55 rune-bearing pages and nine fixed 12-rune openings. This is 33,990 page-and-key cases.
browser_followups.limitation: This browser replay has no saved results yet. It repeats one named variant within the historical 6,272-setting test and does not import its output receipts or change its negative finding. The other folding variant and both rotating schedules are outside this recipe. It does not test general readability, new keys, later text positions, other arithmetic signs or other restart rules.

# Rotating and folded wordlist keys

Can the 43 archived keys recover a familiar 12-rune opening if each key changes shape as it repeats?

## Finding

**No exact opening match.** We tested **6,272 key schedules** at every phase of their actual repeating cycles on the 55 rune-bearing unsolved pages. Their **3,104,640 comparisons** with nine fixed known-reading openings produced zero exact matches. The closest opening agreed for four runes. This is a narrow exclusion of the stated keys, schedules, positions and target readings; it does not judge other plaintext openings.

![For key-01, left rotation changes the next nine-rune cycle; folding walks back through key positions.](experiments/records/rotating-folded-key-openings/clock.svg)

The diagram shows the *key position* used at each of the first 12 ciphertext runes for the first archived key. A left rotation uses slots 0–8 once, then begins the next cycle at slot 1. Folding goes forward and then back. We also tested right rotation and a fold that does not repeat either end. For each key, we reduced identical repeated cycles to their true period before testing every phase. The result file separates **6,272 declared settings** from duplicated 12-step clocks; variants are counted independently because they specify different rules.

## Scope and reproduction

The key list is the 43-rune-key list pinned in the [public wordlist replay](#/experiments/public-wordlist-vigenere). Each page starts its own clock. Non-rune marks do not advance it; each output is the ciphertext rune index minus the scheduled key index modulo 29. We compare only the first 12 runes with the nine openings selected before this test. The original public attempt used ordinary repeating keys; **these rotating and folded schedules are new tests here**, not a claimed historical replay. They do not test other keys, shifts, word resets, interruptions or a language score.

The [manifest](experiments/suites/classical-key-schedules/manifest.json) fixes the schedules and inputs. [Results](experiments/records/rotating-folded-key-openings/results.json) retain per-variant totals, planted recovery controls and a digest of every decoded page start. From the repository root, run `python experiments/records/rotating-folded-key-openings/run.py --check` and `python experiments/suites/classical-key-schedules/check.py rotating-folded-key-openings`. The independent checker rebuilds runes from page JSON and computes the schedules separately.
